I'm driving a 2022 Ram 3500 Dually, and I had a 14,000-pound trailer attached when I filmed this video. I tested several versions today! I feel that this Dev-C3 is the best. Its driving model is ND2. Driving from Las Vegas back to Los Angeles at night. Thank you very much to the author! I also provide some problems I found, and I hope you can improve it! 1. When the trailer is attached, there will be a "ping-pong" situation in some specific situations, a, some curves where the road surface is not flat enough. B, some curves that require greater steering torque (maybe adding Openpilot's Ram-max-tq here will improve it?) C, some curves with narrow lanes. In general, some curves are still not smooth enough when entering and passing the corner with a trailer attached. 2, because my Ram 3500 is Dually, and I replaced it with wider tires, the body is particularly wide. The straight-line driving is very close to the white line on the right side of the road. But generally speaking, it rarely crosses the line, I like it very much! 3. When driving in a straight line, if I switch to the left lane to overtake a large truck in the right lane, I hope my car can get closer to the left side of my lane. Because sometimes the distance is too close when overtaking the vehicle on the right. Finally, to summarize: 1. When hanging a trailer, you need to optimize the control method to avoid "death swing" or "ping-pong". 2. Optimize the steering wheel torque of Ram to make its towing control more stable. 3. Optimize the distance between vehicles when overtaking in the lane

If you're stopped at a red light, and that light turns green, but the next light is still red, it won't move forward (still indicates a red light.
